text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: GPU nodepool 'west-2-gpu-pool' reporting 100% alloc and 12 Pending GPU pods across clusters/west-2a/west-2b. pods stuck Pending: InsufficientGPU.

alex: seeing it, UI shows cluster-autoscaler at max nodes for that nodegroup. any recent changes to quotas? :eyes:

mira: nothing touched on quotas. I deployed a model batch job ~30m ago that ramps to 40 replicas — could be related.

oncall: I'm on it, grabbing nodepool status.

kevin: `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=west-2-gpu-pool -o wide` shows 6 nodes, all 8 GPUs in use, some pods in CrashLoopBackOff. packet loss to one AZ earlier.

sam: runbook step 1: cordon new nodes then drain a couple of crashlooping pods to free GPU if safe. anyone confirm which pods are safe to evict?

alex: quick check: crashlooping pods are from nightly-batch-transformer job; safe to evict. they restart back into Pending though unless capacity freed.

mira: I'm scaling the batch job down to 4 replicas now. patching deployment. `kubectl scale deploy/nightly-transform --replicas=4`

monitoring-bot: Event: cluster-autoscaler: reached nodegroup max size (max=6). Not scaling further.

oncall: autoscaler max is set by infra policy. we hit that cap. request to increase temporary max to 12?

kevin: I'll open a quick PR to bump max. also we should verify cloud provider quota for GPU instances in west-2.

sam: while PR is in flight, manual emergency mitigation: create 2 spot-backed nodegroups in west-2b with taint gpu-temporary=true:NoSchedule and scale them to 3 nodes each so we can drain and move jobs. I can spin those up.

alex: be careful with spot churn. but short-term it's fine. make sure autoscaler doesn't target them (use taint + tolerations for a few pods).

infra-bot: ACTION: created emergency nodegroup 'ephemeral-gpu-b' (3 nodes) - provisioning started. Cloud provider ETA ~5m.

mira: batch job scaled down, some inference pods resumed on freed GPUs, Pending count dropped to 3.

monitoring-bot: Pod restart storm detected: 14 restarts in 10m for job/nightly-transform — investigating image pull/backoff loops.

oncall: good catch. I'm patching liveness probe threshold to be more lenient for the job to avoid thrashing. `kubectl patch deployment/nightly-transform -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"transformer","livenessProbe":{"failureThreshold":10}}]}}}}'`

kevin: Cloud quota check: current GPU vCPU/quota allows +8 instances; we can request emergency quota bump but will take hours. For now ephemeral spot nodegroup is the fastest route.

alex: ephemeral nodes are up, Kube registered them. manually annotated to exclude from cost reporting: `kubectl annotate node <name> cost-tier=ephemeral`

mira: moving safe inference slices to ephemeral nodes via nodeSelector and toleration. patch applied. Pending pods now scheduling, GPU utilization easing.

monitoring-bot: GPU pending count: 0 -> 2 -> 0 over 6m. latency spike for some customers saw 200ms -> 900ms during move. Logged to incident.

oncall: rolling summary for postmortem: root cause = runaway nightly-batch ramp + liveness thresholds causing pod thrash + autoscaler hard cap. mitigations = scale batch down, create ephemeral spot nodegroups, bump autoscaler cap PR, adjust liveness. next steps = request quota bump, add alert for autoscaler hitting max, add preemption policy for batch jobs to avoid stealing inference GPUs.

kevin: PR to bump nodegroup max submitted: infra/ops#452. tagging @oncall for quick review.

sam: created incident doc skeleton and added timeline. will put cost estimate for ephemeral nodes (~$1.8k for 3h) and customer impact window (09:12-09:48 UTC).

mira: postmortem actions: 1) enforce runbook limits on batch ramps 2) add autoscaler max-used alert 3) make batch jobs tolerant of node loss via backpressure 4) automate ephemeral nodegroup creation for emergency.

alex: thanks all. marking incident as: mitigated. I'll follow-up in a couple hours with RCA draft. :white_check_mark:

monitoring-bot: Incident closed: mitigations applied and services stabilized.
